groups.title: Oral Solution (A92400ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins B1, B2 and B6 in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding and when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, and for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, shoulder pain and the like), beriberi, eye fatigue, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 bottle per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if the user is a premature baby or a young child.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may turn the urine yellow and may affect the results of clinical tests. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with levodopa.

If nausea, vomiting, loose stools or diarrhoea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins B1, B2 and B6, and relief of neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, beriberi, eye fatigue, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis

summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Capsule (D23800ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis may occur when a medicine containing pseudoephedrine is taken. If symptoms such as fever, erythema and many small pustules are seen, stop taking this medicine and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with pseudoephedrine; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache); or if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.

If it is to be given to a child under 2 years of age, consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like), another antitussive-expectorant, a cold medicine, an antihistamine, a sedative or alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; rarely signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters over the whole skin or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; liver function disorder (general lassitude, jaundice with yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes); interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever); or posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance and the like).

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of cold symptoms (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint and muscle pain)

groups.title: Cream (102937CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for herpes simplex virus infections (including initial and recurrent genital herpes and cold sores of the lip).
groups.usage: Apply it to the affected area 5 times in 1 day, at intervals of about 4 hours. Treatment must be continued for 5 days; if the condition has not healed after 5 days of use, it may be used for a further 5 days.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you are breast-feeding, or if the user is a child.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an immune deficiency such as AIDS or a bone marrow transplant, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.

Start treatment as early as possible; in recurrent cases start it when the first warning symptoms or lesions appear. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not use this medicine to prevent transmission to other people or to prevent recurrent herpes simplex infection. Do not use it as a base for diluting or mixing other medicines. Use this medicine externally only. Do not use it in the eye, on the cornea or on mucous membranes. To prevent the medicine from spreading to other parts of the body or infecting other people, apply it while wearing a finger cot or rubber gloves.

Consult a pharmacist if you are being given probenecid.

Discomfort such as tenderness, a temporary burning sensation, mild pain including stinging, contact dermatitis, erythematous rash, eczema and allergic reactions and, occasionally, irritation at the site of application, itching, vulvitis, facial swelling, skin discoloration, urticaria, rash, vesicular rash and peeling of the skin may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Herpes simplex virus infections, including initial and recurrent genital herpes and cold sores

groups.title: Oral Solution (D48300ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach, a feeling of a blocked stomach, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, acid eructation (sour belching), loss of appetite, indigestion and overeating.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and older: take 1 bottle per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: 2/3 bottle per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Ages 8 years to under 11 years: 1/2 bottle per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Ages 5 years to under 8 years: 1/3 bottle per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Ages 3 years to under 5 years: 1/4 bottle per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Take it after meals, with an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age, if you have hypersensitivity to caramel, if you have kidney impairment, or if you are on a sodium-restricted diet.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking any other medicine.

If constipation or diarrhoea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (745600ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of itching of the eyes, watering eyes, runny nose, itching of the nose or throat, sneezing, blocked nose and congestion of the sinuses.
groups.usage: Ages 2 to 6 years (11 to 21 kg): take 5 mL (1 teaspoonful) per dose. Ages 6 to 12 years (22 to 43 kg): take 10 mL (2 teaspoonfuls) per dose. Ages 12 years to adult (44 kg and over): take 20 mL (4 teaspoonfuls) per dose. Take it every 4 to 6 hours and do not take more than 4 doses in 24 hours. Do not give it to a child under 2 years of age; if it is really necessary, see a doctor.
groups.caution:
If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a pharmacist.

This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Do not take this medicine if you are being given a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI - some medicines for depression, mental and emotional disorders and Parkinson's disease) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have heart disease, high blood pressure, thyroid disease, diabetes, glaucoma, or a breathing disorder such as asthma or chronic bronchitis, or if you are taking a sedative or a tranquilliser.

Do not exceed the recommended dose. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care. If symptoms do not improve after about 7 days of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with a sedative or a tranquilliser.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: a sore throat lasting 2 days or more, or a sore throat with headache, fever, rash, nausea or vomiting; acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP) or other severe skin adverse reactions with fever, erythema and many small pustules; anxiety, dizziness or insomnia; ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like); or symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance and the like).

summaryTable.What it is for: Temporary relief of itchy or watering eyes, runny nose, itchy nose or throat, sneezing, blocked nose and sinus congestion

groups.title: Enteric-Coated Tablet (D47900ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 to 3 tablets per dose, 1 time in 1 day, at bedtime (on an empty stomach). For the first dose take the smallest amount and then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like), intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a child aged 10 years or younger; if you have an allergic constitution; if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; or if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist. Do not chew the tablets when taking them.

Do not take it together with an antacid. Avoid taking it within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Constipation and the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal intestinal fermentation and haemorrhoids that accompany it

groups.title: Cream (346000CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eczema and dermatitis (atopic dermatitis, contact dermatitis, allergic dermatitis, seborrhoeic dermatitis) with secondary bacterial infection.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount gently to the affected area 3 times in 1 day. On areas where the skin is broken it is better to apply it less often. Treatment with this medicine is limited to 2 weeks.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have a skin infection (cutaneous tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, tinea, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice); if you have eczematous otitis externa with perforation of the eardrum; if you have ulcers (except Behcet's disease); if you have deep second-degree or more severe burns or frostbite; if you have perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris or rosacea; or if the user is a young child under 3 years of age.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if the user is a child.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Do not use it in the eye; if it gets into the eye, rinse the eye immediately with water. Do not use it for purposes other than treatment, such as after applying make-up or shaving. Do not use it under an occlusive dressing without a doctor's supervision.

If any of the following occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: impetigo contagiosa, folliculitis, viral infection, boils, skin irritation, stinging, fever, a burning sensation, rash, reddening of the skin, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, heat rash, worsening of a wound, pressure sores, pustulosis, oedema, worsening of eczema, or raised eye pressure and glaucoma (blurred vision, visual disturbance) when it is used on the skin of the eyelid. Because of systemic absorption, reversible Cushing's syndrome, high blood glucose, diabetes and visual disturbance may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Eczema and dermatitis (atopic, contact, allergic, seborrhoeic) with secondary bacterial infection

groups.title: Soft Capsule (B29800ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins A, C, B1 and E in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness and in old age; for the relief of dryness of the eyes; for night blindness (difficulty seeing at night); for the relief of pigmentation caused by sunlight or skin disease (melasma, freckles); for the prevention of bleeding gums and nosebleeds; and for the relief of peripheral circulatory disturbance and of stiffness of the shoulder and neck, numbness and coldness of the hands and feet at the menopause.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day may cause birth defects. Women who are within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant must not take it.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to soybean oil, soybean or peanut, or if the user is a baby under 12 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have hyperoxaluria (a state in which an excessive amount of oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment, hypoproteinaemia, gout or kidney stones; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; if you have a tendency to thrombosis (blockage of a blood vessel); or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before using it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, an anti-aldosterone medicine, triamterene or an intravenous lipid preparation. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, loose stools, stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary oedema, or menstruation that comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or lasts a long time occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins A, C, B1 and E, relief of dry eyes, night blindness, pigmentation, prevention of bleeding gums and nosebleeds, and relief of peripheral circulatory disturbance and menopausal symptoms

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of discomfort, a burning sensation and itching caused by haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Adults: apply it directly to the affected area up to 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child aged 12 years or younger, or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine only on the anal area and do not use it in the eye.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antihypertensive medicine or an antidepressant.

If reddening of the skin, swelling, irritation or bleeding occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E36200ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamin E in old age, for the relief of peripheral circulatory disturbance and of stiffness of the shoulder and neck, numbness and coldness of the hands and feet at the menopause, for muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency, and for the supply of selenium.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to soybean oil, soybean or peanut; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5; if a particular risk is expected from fat overload; or if you have a tendency to thrombosis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, red patches, asystole (stopping of the heartbeat), reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, vomiting, or menstruation that comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or lasts a long time occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (A11700CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for inflammatory skin disease and seborrhoeic dermatitis.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area, 2 to 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have syphilis or tuberculosis; if you have a skin infection (herpes zoster, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice); if you have had an adverse reaction after vaccination; or if you have a fungal infection, perioral dermatitis or rosacea.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if the user is a child, or if you are an older person.

Use this medicine externally only.

If any of the following occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: because of systemic absorption, visual disturbance, blurred vision, cataract, glaucoma or central serous chorioretinopathy, suppression of pituitary-adrenocortical function; impetigo contagiosa, folliculitis, candidiasis, tinea, viral infection, boils, skin irritation, stinging, fever, a burning sensation, rash, reddening of the skin, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, heat rash, miliaria, worsening of a wound, pressure sores or pustulosis. Rarely, allergic skin reactions and nervous hypersensitivity reactions may occur.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E64500ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and sputum.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. For babies and young children aged 7 years or younger, give a syrup preparation instead. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with another antitussive-expectorant, a cold medicine, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine) or a sedative. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins D, B1, B2 and B6 in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in old age; for the prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and of rickets; for beriberi and eye fatigue; for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulder and the like), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; and for the supply of zinc.

groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, hypercalcaemia, sarcoidosis, kidney disease, kidney stones or severe renal failure, or if the user is a baby under 12 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if the child gets a lot of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you are being given a cardiac glycoside; or if you have had kidney stones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. It may turn the urine yellow and may affect the results of clinical tests.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Taking it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene may cause high blood potassium, so take care. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have hyperoxaluria (a state in which an excessive amount of oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have gout or kidney stones; if you are short of folic acid; or if you have a tendency to thrombosis (blockage of a blood vessel).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting the results of clinical tests. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If discomfort in the stomach or upper abdomen, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary oedema, or menstruation that comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or lasts a long time occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E40200ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins B2 and B6 in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding and when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, and for the relief of angular cheilitis (inflammation at the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to soybean oil, soybean or peanut, or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; or if a particular risk is expected from fat overload.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may turn the urine yellow and may affect the results of clinical tests. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with levodopa.

If nausea, loss of appetite or a feeling of fullness in the abdomen occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-Coated Tablet (E74100ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve constipation and the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 2 times in 1 day, in the morning and in the evening on an empty stomach (before meals or between meals).
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; or if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not chew the tablets when taking them. Children aged 10 years or younger must not take this medicine.

Do not take it within 1 hour after taking an antacid or drinking milk.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, or if constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D51001ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, back pain, headache, menstrual pain, inflammation and pain after injury, and fever and pain caused by influenza.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose with water every 4 to 6 hours; up to 6 tablets (1200 mg as ibuprofen) may be taken in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have peptic ulcer or a severe blood disorder; if clotting must not be interfered with or if bleeding must be stopped; if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have or have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if it is for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you have or have had myocardial infarction; or if you are pregnant.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had peptic ulcer, liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have cardiac insufficiency; or if you are an older person.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with baclofen or methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist if you are taking another antipyretic analgesic, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, digoxin, phenytoin, an antihypertensive, a diuretic, an ACE inhibitor, furosemide, aspirin, lithium or an oral anticoagulant (warfarin and the like).

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: nausea, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, stomach pain, heartburn, loss of appetite, diarrhoea, constipation, vomiting, gastritis, excessive occult bleeding; rarely ulcer of the digestive tract with bleeding; occasionally central nervous system adverse reactions, headache, depression, vertigo, insomnia, fear, disturbance of consciousness, tinnitus, hearing loss, amblyopia; rarely urticaria, purpura, itching or rash; very rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); photosensitivity reactions (frequency unknown), erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; rarely jaundice or raised GOT, GPT or ALP; rarely aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, autoimmune haemorrhagic anaemia, bleeding, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia or reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time); or rarely acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine and other symptoms, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, or high blood potassium.

groups.title: Tablet (E61900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, during and after an illness, during growth and in old age; for the prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and of rickets; for the relief of angular cheilitis (inflammation at the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema and dermatitis; and for the supply of zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day, after a meal.
groups.caution:
Women who are within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant must not take 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have hypercalcaemia, sarcoidosis, kidney disease, high blood potassium, Wilson's disease, kidney stones or severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are under treatment by a doctor; if the child gets a lot of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you have hyperoxaluria; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you are being given a cardiac glycoside; if you have gallbladder disease, liver disease, alkalosis, peptic ulcer or gout; or if you have or have had kidney stones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Consult a doctor, an oriental medicine doctor, a pharmacist or an oriental medicine pharmacist when taking it. The vitamin A contained in this medicine is supplied sufficiently by a normal diet, so the supplementary dose must not exceed 5,000 IU a day.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it. Women taking an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen should take care, because the risk of thrombosis may be increased. Taking it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene may cause high blood potassium, so take care.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, loose stools, stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, upper abdominal pain, coma, red patches, asystole (stopping of the heartbeat), reduced central nervous system function, high blood potassium, wind, stomach pain, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance or pulmonary oedema occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

For other details, check the detailed approved product information.

groups.title: Capsule (428500ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and sputum.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are breast-feeding; if the user is a baby or young child aged 3 months or older and under 2 years; if you are an older person, physically weak, have a high fever or have difficulty passing urine; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, oedema or glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like); or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like), another antitussive-expectorant, a cold medicine, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine) or a sedative. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with a potassium-containing preparation, a liquorice-containing preparation, a preparation containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, a loop diuretic (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or a thiazide diuretic (trichlormethiazide). Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, pseudoaldosteronism (reduced urine volume, swelling of the face, hands or feet, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, raised blood pressure or headache) or myopathy (weakness, cramp of the limbs, paralysis) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Eye Drops (B26100COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eye fatigue, conjunctival congestion, discomfort of the eye after swimming or when dust or sweat gets into the eye, inflammation of the eye caused by ultraviolet or other light, soreness of the eyelid, discomfort while wearing hard contact lenses, itching of the eye, and blurred eyes (when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 3 drops per dose, 3 to 6 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to eye medicines, severe eye pain or glaucoma.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. Do not use it as a wetting solution for soft contact lenses or while soft contact lenses are in the eye. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others. Do not use it after the expiry date, and once opened use it as soon as possible. If symptoms do not improve, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If redness of the eye, itching or swelling occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.
